approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock metrics are a useful capture layer for dashboard history because they can run off-hours, store repeatable values, and support later visualization without repeatedly recalculating expensive operational queries.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Metric, MetricValue, and Schedule columns that support scheduled metric capture and later dashboard visualization.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For dashboard speed, expensive journey analytics can be calculated into a persisted dataset on a schedule rather than recalculating all historical engagement data on each page load.

notes: Read-only SQL verified PersistedDataset exists with refresh interval, schedule, result data, cache, Lava command, and build script columns.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: In Rock Mobile's Content block, Dynamic Content pulls fresh content from the server on each page initialization; static content is bundled into the shell, requires a deploy to update, and processes Lava without `CurrentPerson` context.

Rock v19 materializes recurring iCal schedule occurrences into ScheduleDate rows so date-based SQL and Lava queries can avoid repeatedly expanding recurrence rules. Use the generated dates rather than inventing a separate recurrence expansion process.

source_refs.title: 3 Underrated Features Churches Are Overlooking | Ep 217

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock Mobile documentation marks which Lava filters can run locally in the shell; in XAML-producing Lava, escape user-entered text, URLs, and other strings that may contain characters such as `&` or `'`.
Rock's Lava API guidance identifies Apple TV and Roku channels as examples of custom APIs that can be built with Lava, but warns that Lava webhooks do not include security by default.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified the Lava webhook handler matches active defined values by URL/method, reads Template and EnabledLavaCommands, and renders Lava without an explicit permission check in the inspected handler path.

The Apple TV/Roku API example portion remains official-source-backed; this verification confirms the local handler security caveat and reinforces that agents must inspect configured webhooks before using Lava APIs operationally.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Lava tools should return structured AgentToolResult values and use the dedicated filters for instructions, compact history content, metadata and Rock reference routes. Parameters should be explicit and sanitized, and the built-in tool logs should be used to inspect calls, inputs and results during debugging.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: LMS activity completion can interact with existing Rock concepts such as groups, group sync, and workflow actions, which makes LMS useful for volunteer training and operational follow-up.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LMS activity/completion tables, group/member tables, and workflow action surfaces that can support volunteer-training follow-up.
This verifies structural surfaces only, not a specific LMS implementation.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: In a Lava Entity command, parameter values such as `where` must be wrapped in single quotes; when `id` is also supplied, Rock ignores `where`, `dataview`, and `dynamicparameters`.

Rock v19 materializes recurring iCal schedule occurrences into ScheduleDate rows so date-based SQL and Lava queries can avoid repeatedly expanding recurrence rules. Use the generated dates rather than inventing a separate recurrence expansion process.

source_refs.title: 3 Underrated Features Churches Are Overlooking | Ep 217

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Advanced HTML blocks are powerful CMS surfaces because they can combine markup, Lava, context, and sometimes enabled commands; treat edit access as privileged.

notes: Read-only SQL verified block, block type, attribute, attribute value, and Auth surfaces needed to treat Advanced HTML edit access as privileged.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock v19 adds a contains parameter to the Lava where filter for partial field matching rather than only equality comparisons. Confirm case, type and performance behavior with current Lava documentation before using it in broad queries.

source_refs.title: New Features & Enhancements Coming to v19

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock Roku pages display custom Lava-driven content as part of the application and render SceneGraph-oriented output rather than normal Rock CMS HTML.

Prompt context is layered across Rock's core prompt, organization prompt, agent instructions, skill instructions and current-person context. The practical guidance is to keep each layer concise, add instructions only when testing shows they are needed and pass IdKeys rather than raw integer identifiers.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Apple TV pages in Rock must output valid TVML and can use Rock-provided Lava merge fields such as CurrentPerson, Context, Campuses, SiteStyles, and CurrentPage.

In `workflowactivate`, any key and value beyond the command parameters is treated as a workflow or activity attribute value for the matching attribute key; the supplied value must use that field type's stored-value format.

`CreateShortLink` accepts optional settings in this order: token, site ID, overwrite, random length, category ID, and pinned flag; invalid settings may fall back to defaults, while an empty URL or no shortening-enabled site returns an empty string.

Custom tools should use clear verb-and-entity names and intentionally shaped result types such as Lookup, List, Get, Summary, Insights, AvailableAttributes and AddOrUpdate. Tool names, parameters and bounded result shapes help the model choose correctly and avoid filling its context window with unnecessary data.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The summit's SQL-based Lava examples were intentionally simplified teaching examples. Production tools should prefer cache objects or entity commands when appropriate, return only needed fields, enforce authorization and consider business logic and query cost before choosing SQL.

source_refs.title: RockIQ Rapid Fire Q&A from the AI Summit | Ep 218

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Lava Commands can bypass Rock's built-in security and business logic, so each execution surface should explicitly enable only the commands it needs; HTML blocks start with no commands enabled unless configured.
When reviewing an Advanced HTML block, inspect page/block security, enabled Lava commands, query-string or context inputs, and whether the output exposes sensitive entity data.

notes: Read-only SQL verified the connected instance has page, block, block type, Auth, and block attribute surfaces needed to inspect Advanced HTML block risk.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: An LMS class can combine content acknowledgements, required video watching, quizzes, file uploads, and facilitator-scored activities, so training design should define both learner actions and staff review responsibilities.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LMS activity, class activity, completion, participant, comment, points, grading, file, and notification columns that support structured learner and facilitator actions.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Helix is a Rock web-development surface that combines HTMX, Lava Applications, Lava Commands, and Control Shortcodes as an evolution of Lava-driven web development.

Rock's agent model separates agents, skills and tools, with configuration and security boundaries at each layer. Chat versus MCP and Internal versus Public are separate design choices, and only authorized tools should be exposed to the model for the current person and agent.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The summit strongly warns against allowing an agent to generate and execute arbitrary SQL at runtime because that bypasses Rock security and business logic. Reviewed static SQL inside a narrowly secured Lava tool is distinguished from giving the model an open-ended SQL execution capability.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock LMS organizes training into programs, courses, class instances, learning plans, activities, and learning participants, with the program deciding whether the experience is on-demand or academic-calendar based.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Rock LMS program, course, class, activity, participant, semester, completion, and configuration-mode surfaces.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The Lava Application Content block automatically registers HTMX, and its templates can call an application endpoint with `^/application-slug/endpoint-slug` instead of hard-coding the full `/api/v2/lava-app/1/...` route.
The new communication wizard should be treated as a major workflow change for senders, template managers, and communication trainers.

notes: Read-only SQL verified communication, template, and communication-flow surfaces relevant to treating the communication wizard as a sender/template workflow change.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Advanced HTML Block adds public-safe guidance for CMS security and Lava review: block authorship is privileged, and agents should inspect enabled commands, context inputs, and page/block authorization.

notes: Read-only SQL verified HTML Content and Advanced/CMS block surfaces, enabled Lava command attributes on content-channel blocks, page/block, and Auth surfaces for privileged block review.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: When BI reports are embedded back into Rock, teams still need to honor external licensing and put report pages behind appropriate Rock security roles.

notes: Read-only SQL verified pages, blocks, and Auth rows used to put embedded report pages behind Rock security roles.
This does not verify external BI licensing.
